question: Why do Sadāśiva and other levels draw in powers only partially?
premises: Sadāśiva and other levels serve the lower range because they lack full upward pervasion.
Their contemplative scope is therefore limited.
They draw in powers according to the nearness or distance of their contemplation.
inference: Limited levels of divinity encompass only those powers that fall within their restricted range of contemplation.
uncertainties: The hierarchy implied by 'serving the lower' is doctrinally technical and only lightly glossed here.
plain_english: But Sadāśiva and others, lacking full upward pervasion and oriented to the lower, would draw in powers only according to the nearness or distance of their contemplation.
